title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: LoRA and QLoRA
summary: Full fine-tuning needs about 16 bytes of GPU memory per parameter. LoRA freezes the model and learns a low-rank update ΔW = BA for chosen matrices, training well under 1% of the parameters; QLoRA also stores the frozen base in 4-bit NF4. This lesson does the parameter and memory arithmetic and covers choosing rank, targets and how adapters are merged and served.
objectives: Explain why a fine-tuning update can be low-rank and write the LoRA reparameterisation W' = W + (α/r)BA
Count trainable parameters as r(d_in + d_out) per adapted matrix and for a whole model
Compute training memory for full fine-tuning, LoRA and QLoRA for a 7B model
Describe NF4 quantisation with block-wise scales and double quantisation, and the 4.127 bits per weight it costs
Choose rank, alpha, target matrices and learning rate, and merge or serve adapters
prerequisites: You should know the 16-bytes-per-parameter accounting of training ([Training at Scale](/learn/training-and-adaptation/training-at-scale)), what SFT does ([Instruction Tuning](/learn/training-and-adaptation/instruction-tuning)), and the matrices in a transformer block ([The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block)). Matrix rank is explained briefly where used.
